name: section4b_disk_farkas_thickness_aligned
purpose: A second grid ladder for the same disk benchmark, chosen against the
disk's thickness rather than by halving. It replaces the dyadic ladder as
the basis for the spatial convergence fits; the dyadic one stays because
the reversal it exposes is the evidence for why this one exists.

problem: The isotropic voxel grid spans the disk's 1.75 mm thickness with about
1.75/h cells, and the rim -- where the whole area error lives -- is
resolved only as well as that count. The dyadic ladder resolves the
thickness with 1, 1, 2, 3, 6 and 12 cells: it repeats 1, then skips 4,
5, and 7 through 11. Halving h therefore does not halve the rim error,
and between the first two rungs it does not reduce it at all.
Marching cubes reads 0.757 then 0.636 of exact area across those two,
so refinement moves the answer away from the truth. An analysis gate
excluded them from the fits, which left marching cubes with three error
points spanning one factor of four in h -- too thin to distinguish an
fix: Choose h = 1.75/n. Every rung then resolves the thickness with n cells,
strictly increasing, so no reversal is possible and the gate never
fires. Seven rungs give six error points per representation against the
dyadic ladder's three for marching cubes, over the same range of h.
Trimming the dyadic ladder instead would not have helped: dropping the
two one-cell rungs leaves exactly the four the gate already kept.

why_no_n5_n7_n9_n11: Cost grows like h^-3 while the information gained per rung falls, so
the ladder thins out at the expensive end. n = 2, 3, 4 are nearly free
and are kept adjacent; beyond that every second value is enough to read
n = 14 would be the next rung and is estimated at 83 GB, past what this
machine holds alongside anything else. The per-representation floor in
the driver is set to 0.1458 mm for that reason.
caveat: The grid is positioned by the ground box, not by the disk, so the
thickness spans n or n+1 cells depending on where the disk sits in the
grid. h = 1.75/n makes the count monotone in n, which is what the fits
need; it does not pin it to exactly n.

unchanged_from_the_dyadic_ladder: Scene, benchmark source, and the analytic terminal ratio.
Time step 1.25e-4 s and 400 post-kick frames at 2000 fps.
Reference rule: each representation against its own finest run.
The dt and eps0 sweeps, which this run does not touch.

fitted_from: The dyadic grid sweep's own wall times. Only the two 0.15625 mm runs
were uncontended, so the exponents come from contended runs and are
used for scheduling rather than reported as cost.
cost.memory_gb: 0.032 + 0.162 / h_mm^3, as measured for the dyadic ladder
schedule: 21 runs. All seven tetrahedral rungs together are under two minutes and
3.5 GB. The two coarsest voxel rungs per representation are under a
minute each. The n = 10 and n = 12 rungs hold 166 GB between them and
account for most of the wall clock.
Run with --memory_budget_gb 120 and --solo_gb 200 so nothing is forced
to run alone: about 18 minutes, against 51 serial. A 180 GB budget
reaches the floor of 11 minutes -- the single longest run -- but leaves
too little of the machine free to be worth it.

note: The driver writes manifest.csv with only the cases of one invocation,
truncating rather than merging, so a partial sweep destroys the record
of every earlier one. Runs here merge it back by hand afterwards. That
is a defect in the driver, recorded so the next partial sweep does not
Results share the output directory with the dyadic ladder. The two are
distinguished by rung, not by directory, and both are in the manifest.
